request_text: 대화 내용 뒤에 추가된 게 있는데 그것도 마저 리서치하고 반영한 다음 테스트해줘.
final_prompt_en: An observational school-life photograph of the central woman in an everyday school-life moment. She is a fictional 22-year-old university student, paused in a quiet classroom just before leaving. The supplied portrait guides her visible face and hair: a dark chin-length bob with a softly curved edge, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes beneath straight brows, a soft oval face, and small naturally shaped lips. Her presence feels particular and unforced, with a brief attentive glance toward the photographer while her hands finish their task. She sits sideways on a wooden classroom chair in the aisle beside her desk. Her pelvis rests securely on the chair seat, her left knee points forward, and her left shoe is planted flat on the floor. Her right leg is externally rotated with her right ankle resting across her left thigh just above the knee; the right shoe projects toward the open aisle. Leaning forward from her hips, she holds one lace end in each hand and draws the two ends taut above the tongue of that right shoe. The fingers, two lace ends, shoe tongue, ankle-on-thigh support and grounded left foot read together in the same view. The chair and desk leave open space for her elbows and lifted knee. She wears a pale blue cotton blouse with sleeves casually rolled to her forearms, a cream cable-knit vest, a charcoal pleated skirt falling to the knee, ivory ribbed socks and worn brown leather Oxford shoes. The raised knee organizes the skirt's natural folds, while the rolled cuffs free her wrists for the small task. An open canvas shoulder bag and a closed lecture notebook sit together on the adjacent desktop, ready for her to pick up. Rows of empty desks, a chalkboard with faint erased marks, and tall classroom windows make the academic setting visible. Photograph from a frontal three-quarter position at seated chest height, far enough back to include her complete seated figure, chair support and both shoes. Keep her face and the working hands on the raised shoe large enough to read, with a little aisle floor around the grounded foot. Soft late-afternoon window light shapes her face, the blouse creases and knit texture; the brown wood and pale blue fabric carry the quiet color rhythm. A natural 40 mm perspective and moderate depth of field connect her face, the shoe and the neighboring bag within one inhabited room.

predeclared_criteria_results.evidence: The original image and native face crop retain the dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, straight brows/dark eye relationships, soft oval lower face and small natural lip shape in recognizable relation to the supplied portrait. This is visible reference resemblance, not biometric identity or real age proof.

The skirt-covered pelvis visibly rests on the wooden chair seat; the left lower leg leads to the grounded left Oxford, and the lifted right ankle rests across the left thigh immediately above the knee. Both legs remain continuously traceable. The front of the grounded shoe touches the lower frame, but heel/sole-to-floor support remains visible; no new full-shoe outline gate is added.

Both hands visibly pinch lace-like strands above the same raised Oxford shoe. However, the native hands crop shows a taut horizontal run between the two grips and an additional bow/loop over the tongue; two separate terminal lace ends cannot each be traced unambiguously from one grip to the shoe lacing area. General shoe-tying impression is present, but the declared two-end relation is only partial. No unseen disconnection or deformity is diagnosed.

A pale blue rolled-sleeve blouse appears beneath a cream textured knit vest; charcoal skirt pleats fold around the raised leg, the ivory sock and worn brown Oxford remain legible, and the rolled cuffs leave both acting wrists free. Fine knit stitch count or exact standing hem length is not inferred from the seated image.

Rows of desks, erased chalkboard and classroom windows establish the school room. A canvas shoulder bag and lecture notebooks sit together on the adjacent desk within reach of the seated task, with usable aisle floor visible. The departure reading is supported as an authored interpretation, not proved chronology.
